lines.trans: Classmates, a major accident just broke out during our special concert rehearsal!
Tak Ye-jin was rushed to the hospital with injuries, putting me in a spot where I have to direct instead.
I am supposed to escort VIPs—anyone willing to direct the stage in my place?
Because Ye-jin shoved her clear, Cindy tumbled into the lift opening and got hurt worse.
Why did Ye-jin do that?
In her own way, she was trying to prevent a collision.
And since Ye-jin hurt her own arm too, it feels harsh to scold her over it.
Do you think CEO Byun might threaten to sue us?
I am stuck having to direct the stage myself and nobody in my group chat is replying!
First let's check how things are going at the hospital.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 동기 여러분, 지금 특집 리허설 중 큰 사고가 났습니다!
examples.trans: Classmates, a major accident just broke out during our special concert rehearsal!
Here the word for 'cohort classmates' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (pron).

examples.text: 동기 여러분, 지금 특집 리허설 중 큰 사고가 났습니다!
examples.trans: Classmates, a major accident just broke out during our special concert rehearsal!
Here the word for 'everyone' is key.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: common in TV/radio programming and magazines

examples.trans: There is a special broadcast tonight.
I watched the Lunar New Year special program.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'rehearsal', commonly used in broadcasting and performing arts.

examples.trans: There is a rehearsal before the performance.
The rehearsal starts at 2 p.m.

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.
It really is is loud, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is is loud, so and nice.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 탁예진이 부상으로 병원으로 실려가서 제가 대신 연출을 해야 할 상황입니다.
examples.trans: Tak Ye-jin was rushed to the hospital with injuries, putting me in a spot where I have to direct instead.
Here the word for 'due to injury' is key.

examples.text: 네 매형 병원이 요새 되게 힘들다.
examples.trans: Your brother-in-law's clinic is having a really hard time lately.

examples.text: 병원 문 닫고 네 매형 백수 되게 생겼다니까.
examples.trans: The clinic is about to close and turn your brother-in-law into an unemployed man.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 탁예진이 부상으로 병원으로 실려가서 제가 대신 연출을 해야 할 상황입니다.
examples.trans: Tak Ye-jin was rushed to the hospital with injuries, putting me in a spot where I have to direct instead.
This expression comes from 'was carried off, so'.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Did you hear about this instead of?
I was busy today because of instead of.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 매니저님이 신디 씨 격에 맞게 메인 연출이 와서 설명해주셨으면 좋겠다 그래서 직접 왔네요!
examples.trans: Your manager asked for the main director rather than an assistant to match Cindy's stature, so here I am in person!
Here the word for 'director' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: noun situation

examples.trans: Situation is good.
Situation is bad.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그럼 그 수많은 귀빈들은 누가 의전하니?
examples.trans: Then who is going to escort all those countless VIP guests?
This expression comes from 'will handle VIP protocol for?'.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: We need a producer to direct the stage!
This expression comes from 'to direct'.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 예진이가 미는 바람에 신디가 리프트 구멍에 빠져서 더 다쳤다고 합니다.
examples.trans: Because Ye-jin shoved her clear, Cindy tumbled into the lift opening and got hurt worse.
This expression comes from 'pushing'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 애가 첫 판부터 빵표를 받아서 낙오하는 바람에,
examples.trans: Because she got zero votes right from the opening round and was left behind…
Here the word for 'as a result of' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 커피 마시고 올게, 넌 신디 리프트 스탠바이 해놔, 알았지?
examples.trans: I am grabbing a coffee—get Cindy ready on the stage lift, got it?
Here the word for 'hydraulic stage lift' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예진이가 미는 바람에 신디가 리프트 구멍에 빠져서 더 다쳤다고 합니다.
examples.trans: Because Ye-jin shoved her clear, Cindy tumbled into the lift opening and got hurt worse.
Here the word for 'into the opening' is key.

examples.text: 일반인 훈남한테 빠진 톱스타 같은 거네요?
examples.trans: So it's like a top star falling for an ordinary handsome guy?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 빠지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (fallen for).

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

meanings.note: Used for physical injuries

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 자기 나름대로는 사고를 막아보겠다고 그런 거고요,
examples.trans: In her own way, she was trying to prevent a collision.
Here the word for 'in her own way' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 자기 나름대로는 사고를 막아보겠다고 그런 거고요,
examples.trans: In her own way, she was trying to prevent a collision.
This expression comes from 'trying to prevent'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 네가 회식 가면 본인이 뭐가 되냐고.
examples.trans: She asked what that would make her look like if you showed up at the dinner.
Here the word for 'she herself' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예진이 본인도 팔을 다쳐서 뭐라고 나무라기도 그렇습니다.
examples.trans: And since Ye-jin hurt her own arm too, it feels harsh to scold her over it.
Here the word for 'her arm' is key.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 예진이 본인도 팔을 다쳐서 뭐라고 나무라기도 그렇습니다.
examples.trans: And since Ye-jin hurt her own arm too, it feels harsh to scold her over it.
This expression comes from 'even scolding her'.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Legal Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: I will press charges with the police.
He got sued.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Usually followed by a negative verb to mean 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

meanings.note: 답이 없다 ('there is no answer') is a common idiom meaning a situation is hopeless.

examples.trans: There's really no answer to this problem.
I found the answer to the question.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

examples.text: 예능이 정 하고 싶다면 알아볼게. 근데 그건 안 돼.
examples.trans: If you really want variety, I will look into others. But not that show.

examples.text: 나 가 봐야겠다. 말이 안 통하네. 멤버 다시 알아보세요.
examples.trans: I should leave. We cannot communicate at all. Go look for another cast member.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
